textbookText: x. Brain is more advanced than in amphibians and cranial nerves are 12 pairs. xi. Jacobsons organs are present which detect smell. xii. Fertilization is internal and mostly oviparous. xiii. Eggs are large and yolky; protected by shells which are laid on land. xiv. Development is direct. Youngone develops inside embryonic membrane called amnion, chorion, yolk sac and allantois.

Unique features First land vertebrates, body covered by dry horny scales, body divided into head , neck trunk and tail, two pair of limbs (exception snake), heart-3 chambered, respiration by lungs, metanephric kidney, fertilization internal, young develops in embryonic membrane, 12 pair of cranial nerves.

Class 3: Aves i. They are bipedal, feathery and warm blooded (homeothermic) animals which maintain a constant body temperature and able to fly. ii. Body is streamlined or spindle shaped and divisible into four distinct regions: head, neck, trunk and tail. iii. They have two pair of limbs arising from trunk where fore-limbs are modified into wings. Most of them can fly except flightless birds (e.g., Ostrich). Legs are modified for various purposes like walking, hopping, grasping, perching, wading and swimming. Legs are externally covered by horny epidermal scales. iv. They have uropygium gland (preen gland or oil gland) at the base of the tail, no other skin gland is present. v. The upper and lower jaws are modified into toothless beak. Beaks are adapted to various ways of feeding; seed-picking, fruit-scooping, flesh-tearing, nectar-sipping, woodchiseling etc. vi. Their endoskeleton is bony and the long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic) to reduce weight. Bone marrow is absent. The skull is monocondylic, i.e., with one occipital condyle. Sternum is with a mid -ventral keel for the attachment of large flight muscles.

vii. The alimentary canal is complete and opens posteriorly by cloacal aperture. Alimentary canal contains additionalchamber such as crop and gizzard. The crop stores and softens the food but gizzard crushes or grinds the food into fine particles. viii. Respiratory organ are lungs which are spongy and non-elastic. Air sacs are connected to lungs. Voice is produced by a special organ called the syrinx.

ix. Birds have four-chambered heart. Renal portal system is reduced. RBCs are oval, nucleated and biconvex structure. x. Excretion occurs through metanephric kidney. They are uricotelic animals. Urinary bladder is absent. xi. They have well developed brain than the reptiles. Cranial nerves are 12 pairs. xii. They have good sense of vision but poor smelling power except kiwi which has good sense of smell. Eyes of bird contain nictitating membrane, sclerotic plate and vascular pecten. Presence of ear opening and middle ear is with single ossicle. xiii. Sexes are separate and sexual dimorphism is well marked. Female has a single and functional left ovary and oviduct. xiv. All birds are oviparous. Eggs are larger, yolky and protected in hard calcareous shell. Four embryonic membranes - chorion, amnion, allantois and yolk sac are found. xv. They are most beautiful creatures showing migratory, courtship, nest building, parental care and territorial behaviour. Unique features Feathers covered body, jaws modified as beak, presences of preen gland, forelimbs modified into wings, lungs with air sac, pneumatic bones, single ovary, urinary bladder absent, yolky eggs
Do you know? Rhea Americana or American Rhea or South American Ostrich is the only bird that has urinary bladder.

Class 4: Mammalia i. They are mostly terrestrial, hair-covered, air breathing, and warm-blooded animals. ii. Body is conspicuously divisible into head, neck, trunk and tail. iii. They have two pair of pentadactylous limbs, each with 5 or fewer digits and limbs are adapted for walking, climbing, burrowing, swimming or flying. Hind limbs are absent in some aquatic forms such as whale and dolphins. iv. Exoskeleton includes horns, hairs, spines, scales, claws nails, hoofs etc. v. Skin contains sweat gland and sebaceous gland, mammary glands. Mammary glands are non-functional in males.
